exercise.name: Dumbbell Low Windmill
aliases: Dumbbell windmill (weight in the low hand)

reference.title: Dumbbell Low Windmill
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (windmill hinge with the dumbbell in the low hand, free arm straight up).

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip hinge with trunk side-bend and rotation; load in the low hand)

breathing.pattern: Inhale and brace before you hinge; breathe out as you stand back up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.4 s down, a short pause, about 2.4 s up

prescription.tempo: Slow: about 2-3 s down, brief pause, 2-3 s up
prescription.progression: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: start light; progress to the overhead windmill once the hinge is smooth.

cues.text: Feet wider than the hips, both turned about 45 degrees to the right. Dumbbell in the right hand at the thigh; left arm straight up, eyes on the left hand.
Push the left hip out and back, then hinge and side-bend to the right; slide the dumbbell down the inside of the right leg.
Pause with the dumbbell near the shin: top arm vertical, chest open, left knee straight, right knee soft.
Drive the hips forward and stand back up the same path, eyes on the top hand.
Stand tall; finish the set, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach the floor
mistakes.fix: Hinge from the hips; mid-shin is plenty.
Keep it locked and stacked over the shoulder.
Push the left hip back; the left knee stays straight.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the eyes to the floor

kinematics.norm: Hip hinge with a side-bend and an open chest; no study defines the angles (clinical opinion)
The top-arm side knee straight, the dumbbell-side knee soft; the hips hinge (clinical opinion)
Slides down the inside of the front leg toward the shin or foot (clinical opinion)
Wider than the hips, turned about 45 degrees toward the dumbbell side (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled, about 2-3 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #14327, Dumbbell Low Windmill, video (movement reference)
Konrad, Schmitz and Denner 2001, neuromuscular evaluation of trunk-training exercises (J Athl Train 36(2):109-118; PMC155519)
McGill, Juker and Kropf, quantitative intramuscular myoelectric activity of quadratus lumborum during a wide variety of tasks (Clinical Biomechanics)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Low-back pain: keep the range small; the hinge and side-bend combine under load.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Hamstring or groin strain: shorten the range.
modify: No weight, or the free hand on a box to shorten the range.
Top arm on the hip instead of overhead if the shoulder is sore.

muscleNotes.obliques_l: The obliques on the top-arm side lower the trunk into the side-bend under control and pull it back up (clinical opinion for the windmill; side-lying lateral flexion drove external oblique to about 98% MVC in Konrad 2001).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Quadratus lumborum and the erector spinae hold the trunk as it hinges and bends; quadratus lumborum is a primary lateral stabiliser (McGill, Juker and Kropf).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Both glutes control the hip hinge and drive the stand-up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Both glutes control the hip hinge and drive the stand-up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the chest open toward the top hand (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steadies the pelvis over the planted feet as the hips shift (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Steadies the pelvis over the planted feet as the hips shift (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen as the hips hinge over the straight back leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Lengthen as the hips hinge over the straight back leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Holds the empty top arm vertical (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the top shoulder blade rotated up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Centres the top shoulder as the trunk turns under it (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the dumbbell shoulder packed as the weight hangs (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulder girdle under the hanging dumbbell (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Top arm stays stacked over the shoulder
